title: HDMI-to-FPGA Video Bridge
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

open_decisions.decision: Which HDMI receiver device to use — vendor, part, package, and the input/output feature set it must cover.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks only for "a suitable HDMI receiver device" and names no part, vendor or family.

open_decisions.decision: Which form the receiver-to-FPGA video interface takes, and its width, signalling standard, sample rate and synchronisation scheme.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief offers a choice — "decoded pixel data or a parallel/video stream" — and fixes neither option nor any bus width, voltage or timing.

open_decisions.decision: FPGA selection: family, logic capacity, package, ball/pin count, I/O bank count and bank voltages.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires an FPGA on the same board but says nothing about which one or how large it must be.

open_decisions.decision: HDMI connector variant (type, mounting style, orientation, retention/shield strategy) and its placement relative to the board edge.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says "an HDMI connector" without naming a type, part number, footprint or mechanical arrangement.

open_decisions.decision: How EDID storage is implemented — a dedicated non-volatile device versus emulation by another on-board device — plus its DDC addressing, write-protection and update path.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists EDID storage as required but specifies no device, capacity, bus, address or write policy.

open_decisions.decision: What performs configuration control (an on-board controller, the FPGA itself, or an external host over the debug interface) and over which control bus it reaches the receiver and other configurable devices.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names "configuration control" as a required block without saying what implements it or what it controls.

open_decisions.decision: Clocking architecture: how many clock sources, which are crystals/oscillators versus recovered or synthesised clocks, frequencies, jitter budget, and the distribution/PLL topology.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "clocks" and lists clocking as a stressor, but fixes no frequency, source type, count or jitter requirement.

open_decisions.decision: FPGA configuration memory device type and the configuration mode used, including whether the memory is also writable from the USB/debug interface.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires FPGA configuration memory but names no device, interface or configuration mode.

open_decisions.decision: What the USB/debug interface consists of: connector, USB role and speed, whether a bridge device is used, and whether it also carries FPGA programming/JTAG and console traffic.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "a USB/debug interface" as a single phrase and does not decompose it into functions, devices or connectors.

open_decisions.decision: Power architecture: input supply source and voltage range, the set of rails, regulator topologies, current budgets, and any sequencing or ramp-rate constraints.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on power; the rail set is a consequence of parts that have not been chosen yet.

open_decisions.decision: ESD and port-protection strategy on the HDMI interface, including what is protected, the protection technology, and the capacitance budget it may consume on TMDS pairs.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names ESD as an area to treat as critical — a stressor to address, not a device or topology it selects.

open_decisions.decision: Layer stackup: actual layer count and ordering, dielectric materials and thicknesses, copper weights, and which layers serve as reference planes for TMDS and for the FPGA escape.
open_decisions.why_open: Metadata gives 6 as a likely layer count only; the brief fixes no stackup, material or plane assignment, while naming reference planes as critical.

open_decisions.decision: Impedance targets and matching rules: single-ended and differential impedance values, intra-pair skew and inter-pair length-matching tolerances for TMDS and for the video bus.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires TMDS routing to be treated as critical but states no impedance, skew or matching number.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting-hole pattern, keep-outs and whether the board is standalone or mates with a carrier/host.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no mechanical envelope, form factor or mounting requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Video bandwidth target: maximum supported resolution, refresh rate, colour depth and resulting TMDS bit/pixel-clock rate the board is designed to.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says "HDMI video" without naming any resolution, frame rate, colour depth or clock rate; the target is a decision to be made and justified.

open_decisions.decision: Whether HDMI audio is de-embedded and delivered to the FPGA, and whether CEC, ARC/HEAC or the utility pin are supported or left unpopulated.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief scopes the board around video and does not state whether the other HDMI-carried functions are in or out of scope.

open_decisions.decision: DDC and hot-plug-detect topology: whether the HDMI cable-side supply domain is crossed at all and, if it is, how that crossing is handled — sourced, sensed, isolated, level-shifted or left unconnected — together with how HPD is asserted and what the DDC bus carries on each side.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires EDID storage but says nothing about the DDC/HPD electrical topology or whether any voltage-domain crossing is needed to serve it.

open_decisions.decision: FPGA pin assignment and escape plan: which banks carry the video bus, configuration, clocks and debug, and how fanout/escape is achieved on the chosen stackup.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief flags FPGA escape as critical but the FPGA, its package and its pinout are all unchosen, so no escape constraint is yet fixed.

open_decisions.decision: Bring-up and test provisions: test points, status indicators, probe access on the video bus, and any connector or header dedicated to validation.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies no test, debug-visibility or instrumentation requirement beyond the USB/debug interface itself.

open_decisions.decision: Manufacturing constraints: fabricator and capability class, minimum trace/space, via technology (through, blind/buried, via-in-pad), assembly process and sides populated.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no vendor, process or capability limit; these follow from the stackup and escape decisions, which are themselves open.
